title: Boy Toy
author: Barry Lyga
current_text: Resident Julie Porter challenged Boy Toy, alleging that it had been acquired with public funds in violation of the law; Superintendent William Harbron denied her removal request, and a staff committee recommended keeping the book. The Dover School Board unanimously voted to keep Boy Toy at the Alumni Drive school after taxpayer Julie Porter requested reconsideration.

sources.quote: The appeal, made by resident Julie Porter, follows Superintendent William Harbron's denial of her initial request to have the book "Boy Toy" by Barry Lygra removed, alleging the material was acquired with public funds in violation of the law.
sources.title: School Board meets Wednesday to consider whether a book should be removed from high school library

sources.quote: As per School Board policy KEC, Harbron asked a staff committee to review the book. Assistant Superintendent Christine Boston, who chaired the committee, said they unanimously recommended keeping the book in place as "removing this book would prevent access to ideas, viewpoints and opinions for all students based on the opinions of some." Harbron agreed with and adopted the staff committee’s report, after which the appeal to the School Board followed.
sources.title: School Board meets Wednesday to consider whether a book should be removed from high school library

sources.quote: The seven-member Dover School Board voted unanimously on Wednesday night for the book to stay at the Alumni Drive school after taxpayer Julie Porter filed a request for reconsideration of the 2007 title.
sources.title: Dover School Board unanimously rejects effort to ban 'Boy Toy' from library | New Hampshire Public Radio
